The Purpose of the test weight sets will be to conduct load tests of several different types of equipment including but not limited to: • M 88A2 recovery vehicle (70,000 lbs lift capacity) • M88A1 recovery vehicle (50,000 lbs lift capacity) • M7 Forward Repair System (9,900 lbs lift capacity) • HEMTT Wreaker (12,000 lbs lift capacity) • Forklifts (from 4,000 – 27,000 lift capacity) T he scope of this procurement shall be executed in accordance with the following specifications:

atement of Work The Consolidated Maintenance Activity as part of the Minnesota Army National guard has identified a requirement to procure one (1) Stackable Test Weight Sets. The Purpose of the test weight sets will be to conduct load tests of several different types of equipment including but not limited to: • M 88A2 recovery vehicle (70,000 lbs lift capacity) • M88A1 recovery vehicle (50,000 lbs lift capacity) • M7 Forward Repair System (9,900 lbs lift capacity) • HEMTT Wreaker (12,000 lbs lift capacity) • Forklifts (from 4,000 – 27,000 lift capacity) T he scope of this procurement shall be executed in accordance with the following specifications: 1. The stackable weight systems shall be designed such that they can support all of the equipment listed above 2. The set shall include a four-legged sling so that center post / base and the individual weights can be lifted / stacked using a crane. A four-legged sling capable of lifting the maximum weight of the system shall be provided with each weight set. The sling shall be proof loaded to 200% of its rated load by the sling manufacturer. The slings legs shall be of sufficient length so that there is no interference with the sling and the center post / base when placing the first weight on the center post / base. Each individual weigh

. The slings legs shall be of sufficient length so that there is no interference with the sling and the center post / base when placing the first weight on the center post / base. Each individual weight shall have four lifting provisions properly sized for the sling hooks. 3. The weight set shall consist of a center post / base and additional stackable weights. Each item shall have a target weight with a tolerance of -0% / +5 % of the target weight. The following target weights shall be included as part of the system. • 5x 10 00 lbs • 3x 5000 lbs • 5x 10,000 lbs. O ther configurations will be reviewed and considered if they meet the lifting requirements listed above. No individual weight over 20,000 will be considered. 4. The test weight set shall be stackable to achieve the specified weights detailed below. • 4,000 l bs • 5,000 lbs • 10,000 lbs • 12,000 lbs 18 August 2026 • 27,000 l bs • 50,000 lbs • 70,000 lbs 5. T he test weight stack shall be able to interface with a crane hook by directly interfacing with the center post / base. The center post / base interface shall be capable of lifting the test weight stack at its maximum weight (70,000 lb). IREMENTS AND PROCESSES The contractor shall perform all corrosion control, structural repair, and refinishing services in strict accordance with applicable Air Force Technical Orders (TOs), Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) specifications, and the Department of Defense Qualified Products List (QPL). The ultimate standard of acceptable performance is the delivery of structurally sound, safe, and fully operational equipment, restored to a like-new finish, and delivered within the contractually mandated TAT limits. 3.1. CORROSION CONTROL REPAIR PROCESS The contractor shall perform structural repairs in accordance with applicable TOs (Reference PRS-2). The process shall include the following steps: The structural repair process shall be performed as follows: • Assess the extent of damage by visually inspecting the structure for cracks, corrosion, and compromised load-bearing components. • Prepare the area by removing paint and cleaning surfaces to allow for an accurate evaluation. • Removed all damaged material by cutting, sanding, or grinding to ensure only clean, structurally sound material remains. • Fit and install replacement material, use correct alignment, thickness and material compatibility before fastening or welding. • Secure and reinforce the repair using ap

To support resear

Technology (NIST) enables science and industry by providing essential measurement methods, instrumentation, and standards to support all phases of communications technology development, from fundamental characterization and discovery to production. To support research and measurement services in radio frequency and microwave power, the Radio Frequency Technology Division in CTL requires a power sensor that can operate in multiple rectangular waveguide bands . The power sensor will serve as a check standard for power calibrations performed with both connectorized and on- wafer equipment. Only new equipment will be considered. The Purpose of the test weight sets will be to conduct load tests of several different types of equipment including but not limited to: • M 88A2 recovery vehicle (70,000 lbs lift capacity) • M88A1 recovery vehicle (50,000 lbs lift capacity) • M7 Forward Repair System (9,900 lbs lift capacity) • HEMTT Wreaker (12,000 lbs lift capacity) • Forklifts (from 4,000 – 27,000 lift capacity) T he scope of this procurement shall be executed in accordance with the following specifications: 1. The stackable weight systems shall be designed such that they can support all of the equipment listed above 2. The set shall include a four-legged sling so that center post / base and the individual weights can be lifted / stacked using a crane. A four-legged sling capable of lifting the maximum weight of the system shall be provided with each weight set. The sling shall be proof loaded to 200% of its rated load by the sling manufacturer. The slings legs shall be of sufficient length so that there is no interference with the sling and the center post / base when placing the first weight on the center post / base. Each item shall have a target weight with a tolerance of -0% / +5 % of the target weight. The following target weights shall be included as part of the system. • 5x 10 00 lbs • 3x 5000 lbs • 5x 10,000 lbs. The center post / base interface shall be capable of lifting the test weight stack at its maximum weight (70,000 lb). IREMENTS AND PROCESSES The contractor shall perform all corrosion control, structural repair, and refinishing services in strict accordance with applicable Air Force Technical Orders (TOs), Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) specifications, and the Department of Defense Qualified Products List (QPL). DESCRIPTION OF SERVICES: 1.3.1. The contractor shall provide a skilled labor force capable of performing comprehensive corrosion control, including metal repair (welding and fabrication), fiberglass rework, plastic structure restoration, composite repairs, and painting. The contractor shall utilize sufficient surface preparation equipment and methods to remove existing coatings and ensure optimal adhesion and bonding of new paint systems, all while performing corrosion removal without compromising the structural integrity of the assets. All equipment restoration, painting, and coating applications shall be performed in accordance with applicable technical data and Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) regulations. To support resear

Technology (NIST) enables science and industry by providing essential measurement methods, instrumentation, and standards to support all phases of communications technology development, from fundamental characterization and discovery to production. To support research and measurement services in radio frequency and microwave power, the Radio Frequency Technology Division in CTL requires a power sensor that can operate in multiple rectangular waveguide bands . The power sensor will serve as a check standard for power calibrations performed with both connectorized and on- wafer equipment. Only new equipment will be considered. Item Specifications and Quantities: Item 1: Calorimetric Power Meter Quantity: 1 Specifications: 1.1 Power measurements in rectangular waveguide bands spanning frequencies from at least 75 GHz to 1.1 THz. 1.2 Typical relative power measurement accuracy of ±5 % across all supported rectangular waveguide bands. 1.3 Measurement ranges from 1 µW to 200 mW. 1.4 Maximum continuous wave (CW) input power of at least 200 mW. 1.5 Calibration factor switch to adjust the power meter display to correct for input loss or gain. 1.6 Internal calibration capability to heat the sensor element with a known amount of dc power. 1.7 USB port for instrument c

measurement methods, instrumentation, and standards to support all phases of communications technology development, from fundamental characterization and discovery to production.
